name: VPN app, designed badly then fixed
description: Writes a deliberately weak design for a VPN app, then runs a red-team loop: the reviewer tries to break the logic, the fixer applies one change, the snapshot records the iteration in its own folder. Stops when the reviewer stops finding anything that breaks.

product.title: What we are designing
product.default: A VPN client for phones: three onboarding screens, a paywall, a big connect button, and a server list you can pick from.

bar.title: Stop when nothing scores below this

steps.title: Draft it badly on purpose
steps.instruction: You are writing the FIRST version of a design, and it is meant to be bad. Do the obvious lazy thing in every place there is a choice: put everything on one screen, name the buttons with the feature instead of the benefit, ignore what happens when the connection drops, and leave the paywall as a wall with no explanation. Cover the screens that exist for this product, including onboarding, the paywall, the connect button and server selection. Be concrete and specific, not vague -- a vague bad draft cannot be improved. End with the full the first, deliberately bad design, as markdown, in the `markdown` field. Put the whole design, as markdown, in the `markdown` field.

steps.title: Fold it into the design
steps.instruction: The design is in the data below. If `change` is empty this is the first pass: return the design unchanged. If it is not empty, apply that one change and nothing else. Either way output the complete current design as markdown in `markdown` -- not a diff.

steps.title: Keep round 0
steps.instruction: Write the round 0 design into its own folder under the run.

steps.title: Try to break the logic
steps.instruction: You are the reviewer. The current design is in the data below -- read it there, not from memory. Be a user, a lawyer and the person who pays the bill at the same time. Find the things that are actually BROKEN, not merely ugly: states the design does not handle, promises it makes that nothing delivers, moments where a user can get stuck, and anything a subscription would be refused for. For each one say the exact moment it happens and what the user sees. If you genuinely cannot break anything any more, say so and give severity 0. This is round 1.

worst_severity.description: 1 is cosmetic, 5 is the app is unusable or unlawful. 0 means nothing found.

the_fix.description: The single highest-value change. Only if there is something to fix.

steps.title: Fix exactly one thing
steps.instruction: Take the reviewer's findings in the data below and apply the single highest-value change. Change only that; everything else stays. In one line say what you changed. In `markdown`, output the design with that change applied.

steps.title: Carry the fix back to the loop
steps.instruction: The fixed design is in the data below. Write it out, as markdown, into `markdown`, unchanged.

steps.title: Keep this round
steps.instruction: Write the current design into a folder named for this run, so each iteration is kept apart from the others.

steps.title: Smoke test the whole flow
steps.instruction: Walk the finished design end to end as a first-time user: install, pay or not pay, connect, pick a server, lose connection, come back. Write down every point where the user has no idea what to do. This is the last word on whether the design works.

steps.title: Write the report
steps.instruction: Write the final report: the starting design in one paragraph, every round of changes in order with the reason for each, what the reviewer found each time, and the smoke-test verdict. Plain markdown, no preamble.
